primary_source.title: Small Ball Probabilities for Linear Images of High-Dimensional Distributions
primary_source.theorem: Theorem 1.2: normalized sums of independent density-<=K variables have density <=sqrt(2)K

partner_result_applied.scope: Banks transfer for pure physical bipartite quadratic forms and one-pivot Schur square mechanism
partner_result_applied.application: combined its sigma_2 pure-bipartite theorem with the new sigma_1 plus square theorem; strengthened its Schur route by joint conditional smoothing

quantitative_conclusion: For Q=2 alpha X^T B Y+F(X)+r_Y^T Y+c+beta[Z+h(X,Y)]^2, with product X,Y coordinate densities <=1 and independent scalar Z density <=K_Z, ||p_Q||inf <=4sqrt(2) K_Z/sqrt(|alpha beta| sigma_1(B)). For a physical pivot a and Schur complement with one active-side principal block zero and cross B0, ||p||inf<=4sqrt(2)/sqrt(|a|sigma_1(B0)); product >=1 gives <=4sqrt(2).
unresolved_implication: Extract from arbitrary A with three |lambda|>=1 either a valid diffuse-frame branch or a physical pivot whose Schur residual has one zero principal side and |a|sigma_1(B0)>=c, or control the remaining two-sided self-interaction geometry without rotating away independence.
next_step: Test Rudelson-Vershynin large-coordinate removal/tensorization as a structural decomposition tool for the localized spectral frame; in parallel derive a two-sided self-block extension of the joint bilinear-square smoothing theorem.
